Hint: A precious liquid we should conserve.
Explanation: Fix leaks and use water carefully to reduce demand.

Hint: The ability to power lights, machines and movement.
Explanation: Switch off unused equipment and improve efficiency to reduce energy demand.

Hint: Process discarded materials into usable materials again.
Explanation: Sort accepted materials correctly. Local recycling rules determine what belongs in each bin.

Hint: Use an item again instead of throwing it away.
Explanation: Refill, repurpose and choose durable items to reduce demand for new materials.

Hint: This renewable source comes from the sun.
Explanation: Solar technology captures sunlight to supply useful energy.

Hint: Organic scraps break down into a soil amendment.
Explanation: Composting suitable organic waste returns nutrients to soil. Follow your local collection rules.

Hint: The variety of living things and ecosystems.
Explanation: Protecting habitats supports the variety of life, including plants, animals and microorganisms.
Transport and industrial activities can release greenhouse gases and other air pollutants. Not all emissions are visible.

Hint: Fix something so it can be used for longer.
Explanation: Repairing equipment and products can extend their life and prevent avoidable waste.

Hint: Moving air that can turn a turbine.
Explanation: Wind turbines convert moving air into electricity. Wind also moves kites, trees and surface waves.

Hint: A collective term for plant life.
Explanation: Native plants provide habitat and support healthy ecosystems.

Hint: A collective term for animal life.
Explanation: Protecting habitats helps sustain animal populations and the ecosystems they belong to.

Hint: Materials or items that are discarded.
Explanation: Prevent waste first, then consider reuse and recycling before disposal.

Hint: A material used to release energy.
Explanation: Fuel choices and efficiency affect environmental impacts. Sustainable aviation fuel is one approach to reducing aviation lifecycle emissions; it is not emission-free.

Hint: A mark left behind; also a way to describe environmental impact.
Explanation: An environmental footprint describes impacts associated with an activity or product, such as resource use and emissions.
